import { Tabs, TabItem } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

A `file` field holds a file, not a string of characters. The field stores the
id of an artifact, and the artifact store keeps the bytes outside the
document. This keeps documents small and lets two documents share one file
without copying it.

## When to use this

Use a `file` field when the file is part of the record: a signed contract on
a booking, a damage photo on a maintenance ticket, a manual on an item. For
discussion files that belong to no field, use the attachments panel instead
(see [Add comments and attachments](/build/model/relations/comments-attachments/)).

## Before you start

- **Storage is built in.** The [artifact store](/admin/configure/file-storage/) exists on every instance. You
  declare the field; you do not configure storage.
- **A size limit.** One upload is limited to 50 MiB by default
  (`artifact.max_upload_bytes`, 52,428,800 bytes). Your administrator sets
  the limit.
- **A type list, if you want one.** Facet accepts any file type by default.
  Declare an `accept` list when the field should take only some types.

## Steps

<Tabs syncKey="build-mode">
<TabItem label="Builder">

1. Open the doctype in the **Builder** and add a field of type **File**.
2. Optionally enter the **Accept** list as MIME types, for example
   `application/pdf`.
3. Save. The form for the doctype now takes files in that field.

</TabItem>
<TabItem label="Files">

The Brightwater item doctype with a damage photo and a manual added, as a
complete fields extract:

```yaml
# equipment/doctypes/equipment.Item.yml (fields extract)
fields:
  name:
    type: string
    title: Name
    required: true
    filters: [equality, text_search]
  damage_photo:
    type: file
    accept: [image/jpeg, image/png]
    title: Damage photo
  manual_pdf:
    type: file
    accept: [application/pdf]
    title: Manual
```

A field without `accept` takes every file type.

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

### The accept list uses MIME types

Facet decides the type of an upload from the file content, not from the file
name, and rejects an upload that does not match the list. Renaming a file
does not get it past the check.

### Upload in the app

In a form, the user picks a file for the field. Facet uploads the bytes,
stores them, and puts the artifact id into the field. The save and the upload
are one step: if either fails, nothing is written.

### Upload through the API

Send a multipart body. One part named `$content` carries the document fields,
and one part per file field carries the bytes, named after the field.

```sh
curl -k -X POST "https://facet.localhost:3443/Api/equipment/Item" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FACET_API_KEY" \
  -F '$content={"name":"Folding table 6ft"}' \
  -F 'manual_pdf=@./table-manual.pdf'
```

`-k` skips the certificate check of the local development address.

## What the store does

| Rule | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| Same bytes, one copy — mostly | Identical bytes are stored once and reused, when the uploader can already read the stored copy. Two callers who cannot read each other's files each store their own copy. |
| Access follows documents | A file is readable through the documents that reference it. |
| Out-of-band uploads | A file pasted into a long text is uploaded first and linked on save. |

A longtext field can embed a file link with the form
`urn:facet:artifact:<id>`. Every reader of that document gains access to the
file.

## Example

The declaration above gives every item a photo and a manual field. A create
with a manual stores:

```json
{
  "name": "Folding table 6ft",
  "manual_pdf": "01HQ2F5WX8K4M3PZC6NRB9TJVA"
}
```

The value is the artifact id — a 26-character ULID. The document page renders
it as a download link.

## Troubleshooting

### The upload answers `413`

The file is larger than the size limit. Use a smaller file, or ask your
administrator to raise the limit.

### The upload answers `422` with a MIME error

The file content does not match the `accept` list. Convert the file or widen
the list; changing the file name alone does not help, because Facet reads the
content.

### An export carries a short id instead of the file

That is the artifact id. The file content does not travel with a CSV or JSON
export; download files from the document page.

### A file link in a document shows as dead

The file was destroyed by an administrator. The reference stays in the text
but the bytes are gone.
